en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Holy Six-Syllable Great Vidyārāja Dhāraṇī,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Śīladharma, Imperially Appointed Court Disperser and Acting Assistant Director of the Court of State Ceremonial,
Dharma-Transmitting Master, Subject Śīladharma, in accordance with the Imperial Decree.
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the Venerable Ānanda, saying: "Ānanda,
you should listen attentively."
I possess the six-syllable vidyārāja dhāraṇī,
which was proclaimed by immeasurable Buddhas of the past for the sake of all great beings.
Ānanda, I now further proclaim this dhāraṇī for you and for all sentient beings of the final age.
May sentient beings, in future ages, obtain this dhāraṇī.
And they shall obtain great benefit.
At that time, Ānanda, as well as Mahābrahmā, the Lord of the Sahā World, Śakra,
the Four Great Heavenly Kings, and the others—
They addressed the World-Honored One, saying:
"World-Honored One, out of your great kindness and great compassion, we pray that you will proclaim it for us,
so that we and those of the future age may [attain realization]."
Sentient beings shall obtain benefit and peace for a long night. At that time,
the World-Honored One then spoke the Six-Syllable Great Brightness King Dhāraṇī, saying:
Tadyathā: nandile, madumati, maṇḍalike, pūrṇanandike svāhā. At that time, the Buddha addressed Ānanda, saying:
If there are sentient beings who,
upon hearing the names and phrases of this Great Vidyārāja Dhāraṇī,
receive and uphold it with faith, recollecting and reading it aloud.
Furthermore, for those who offer various kinds of worship with incense and flowers,
whatever fears they may have— such as fear of kings, fire, water, and so forth— [shall be dispelled].
Even the terrors of thieves and enemies—
may they be completely liberated from all such fears.
Furthermore, even poisons,
up to and including weapons of war,
will be unable to cause them harm.
Furthermore, there were gods, humans, and non-humans,
as well as yakṣas, rākṣasas, kumbhāṇḍas,
and even kaṭapūtanas and the like.
Neither those possessed by spirits nor those afflicted by malaria can cause them harm.
Furthermore, as for malarial fever:
One day, two days, three days, four days;
or again, many days;
or again, for but a brief moment.
Furthermore, headaches, earaches, backaches, and abdominal pains—
even up to the suffering of various malignant diseases such as dropsy—
none shall be able to afflict them.
Throughout day and night,
they shall constantly obtain peace and security,
and all their aspirations shall be fulfilled.
All shall have their wishes fulfilled.
At that time, the World-Honored One further spoke this dhāraṇī:
*Tadyathā:* 1. Aṇale, 2. Panaṇale, 3. Namina-maṇi, 4. Vakṣe, 5. Kusuke, 6. Kucake, 7. Bhūtāgra, 8. Tejovati, 9. Yaśovati, 10. Svāhā. The Buddha said to Ānanda:
If there are sentient beings who hear this dhāraṇī,
I do not see any among the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, or rākṣasas [who could harm them].
Piśācas, bhūtas, kūṣmāṇḍas, pūtanas, kaṭapūtanas,
and even humans and non-humans.
Regarding all such unbeneficial actions,
should anyone dare to oppose them?
Ānanda, such are the unbeneficial actions of this kind.
If anyone violates this dhāraṇī of mine,
their head shall split into seven pieces,
like the branches of an arjaka tree.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Such is the power and majesty of the merit of this dhāraṇī."
It brings immeasurable and boundless benefit to sentient beings without end;
you should receive and uphold it.
Cause it to be widely disseminated so that,
in future generations,
it shall not be interrupted.
When the Buddha had finished preaching this sutra,
Ānanda, the Great Brahmā King, Śakra Devendra, the Four Heavenly Kings, and the others,
having heard what the Buddha had spoken, [rejoiced].
Rejoicing and receiving it with faith,
they prostrated to the Buddha and withdrew.
Thus concludes the *Sūtra on the Dhāraṇī of the Noble Six-Syllable Great King*.
